confirmed.title: TP-dispatch SLO clock is frozen at tick start and anchored to the first fill: real multi-second delays show as 0.0 s, and an immediate dispatch shows as a 60 s breach. The AC-14 test cannot fail.
confirmed.requirement: NG-CELL-002 (durable TP intent reaches the router <=2 s after the history-fill commit; blockers show queue age and exact reason), AC-14, NG-RISK-002 (TP priority over entries)
confirmed.failure_scenario: (a) 12 BUY cells fill in one tick and each submit/cancel round trip takes 0.4 s. The engine awaits every transport in turn (_submit -> _dispatch_intent at 1864). The 12th TP intent is committed about 4.4 s after the history commit, but tp_latencies records 0.0 and the snapshot shows last/max_latency_s = 0.0. (b) The price spikes above the upper bound while 18 SELL entries fill. _act awaits all 12 OUTSIDE_BOUNDS entry cancels first (1705) and only then commits TP intents (1707+). The first TP intent is committed at +4.8 s and the last at +11.6 s, yet all are recorded as 0.0 latency: entry housekeeping delays exits. (c) AC-05 flow: a fill of 2 at t0 stays below minimum. Then +3 arrives at t0+60 s and TP 5 goes out in that same tick. The snapshot reports last_latency_s = 60.0, a false SLO breach, because the obligation clock kept the first below-minimum fill time.
confirmed.evidence: _apply_history stamps the obligation clock with the tick-start now_ms inside the batch (1241: self.meta.obligations.setdefault(..., now_ms)). _tp_candidates takes since = min(obligations) (1632). _submit computes latency as (now_ms - since_ms) with now_ms = _ms(now) of the same tick start (1794, 1862-1863). So any intra-tick delay is invisible, and setdefault keeps the first fill of the generation even when that obligation was below minimum. Order inside _act: _resume_pending_intents (1662), then _dispatch_cancels (1705), then the sequential TP _submit loop (1707-1717). Each step awaits transport with a 10 s timeout. Measured with scratch experiments exp_slo.py (0.4 s per transport, 12 TPs: submits at 0.4..4.8 s, all latencies 0.0), exp_slo_bounds.py (cancels at 0.4..4.8 s, TPs at 5.2..12.0 s, latencies 0.0) and exp_slo_partial.py (last_latency_s '60.0' for a same-tick dispatch). test_ng_engine_history.py:174-190 asserts latency <= 2, but FakeExchange never advances the clock inside a tick, so that assertion is always true.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Stamp the history commit and each TP intent commit with self.clock() at the moment they happen, not the tick-start now. Start the SLO clock when the obligation becomes dispatchable (the commit of the fill that clears the minimum/blocker). Commit all router-approved TP intents before awaiting any transport, and dispatch TPs before entry cancels. In AC-14, drive a clock that advances during transport.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I reproduced all three scenarios on the real engine with scratch scripts that used FakeExchange and the test harness. engine.py is the same at bcd2eebef and HEAD.

Code facts:
- `_apply_history` stamps obligations with `now_ms`, which is the tick-start time, through `setdefault` (engine.py:1241).
- `_tp_candidates` takes `since` as the minimum of those stamps, again using `setdefault` (engine.py:1632).
- `_submit` records latency as `(_ms(now) - since_ms)`, where `now` is the tick-start value passed down from `tick()` (engine.py:1794, 1862-1863). A delay inside one tick is therefore always recorded as 0.
- Cancels are handled differently: `_dispatch_cancels` uses `self._now_ms()` (engine.py:1944), so only the TP latency metric is frozen at tick start.
- In `_act`, `_dispatch_cancels` (engine.py:1705) awaits every cancel transport before the TP `_submit` loop runs (engine.py:1707-1717). `_submit` commits the durable intent and then awaits the transport for each TP, one after another.

Measured results:
- **(a)** 8 BUY fills in one tick, 0.4 s per submit: the TP venue submits land at +0.4 … +3.2 s. `tp_latencies` records all of them as 0.0, and the snapshot shows last and max latency of '0.0'.
- **(b)** Mid moves to 6.2 (above the upper bound) with 18 SELL fills and 12 live BUY entries: the 12 OUTSIDE_BOUNDS entry cancels run at +0.4 … +4.8 s. The 18 TP submits follow at +5.2 … +12.0 s. Every latency is recorded as 0.0. The durable TP intents are not even committed until 4.4 s or more after the history commit. This happens with the throttler free (20 > 18) and the transport free, since it is only busy with lower-priority entry cancels. That breaks the NG-CELL-002 local-dispatch SLO ("durable TP intent ... не позднее 2 секунд после commit history fill") and the spec's "TP obligations имеют приоритет над entries / Exit obligations всегда обслуживаются первыми".
- **(c)** AC-05 flow: a fill of 2, then 59 more ticks, then +3. TP 5 is dispatched in the same tick as the +3, but the snapshot shows last and max latency of '60.0' against an SLO of 2.0. That is a false breach, because `setdefault` kept the time of the first fill, which was below the minimum.

Why this is reachable in production: the real Lighter port awaits `submit_with_client_id` / `cancel_with_client_id`, which sign and send inside `_tx_lock`. Each call therefore takes a real network round trip, and several fills in one tick are enough to hit this.

The AC-14 test (test_ng_engine_history.py:174-190) only advances the FakeClock between ticks. It cannot see delays inside a tick. It would only catch a delay that spans more than 2 ticks. So "cannot fail" is slightly overstated, but the core of the claim holds.

Why I lowered severity to medium: nothing wrong is sent and no fund-safety invariant breaks. The damage is a seconds-scale TP delay while the price is moving, plus a misleading metric and a test that does not discriminate. That fits medium better than high.

Scratch scripts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikhail/ed31a3df-55bd-475b-8111-912d06f80d1d/scratchpad/exp_slo_check.py and exp_slo_bc.py.

confirmed.title: A history conflict or ledger-invariant freeze on one cell withholds every cell's TP obligations and skips the outside-bounds entry cancels
confirmed.requirement: NG-OPS-001 (pause keeps servicing confirmed TP obligations; a fill gap or unknown blocks only new exposure of the affected cell), NG-HIST-002 (a key with a different payload -> history conflict and pause), NG-RISK-003 (does not abandon TP obligations), NG-OPS-002 (entries are cancel-requested outside bounds)
confirmed.failure_scenario: The venue serves one contradictory trade row for cell A (an overfill on A's CID). The store opens an OVERFILL conflict, tp_blockers becomes ['HISTORY_CONFLICT'] and _act returns early. Cell B is unrelated: its entry fully fills, history is complete and exact, E = 10, and venue net is +10. B still gets no TP for 60 s, and none until an operator runs ack_history_conflict. When the book then leaves the range, no OUTSIDE_BOUNDS cancel is sent: 0 cancels, 9 entries stay live. Any StoreError or LedgerError raised anywhere in a tick behaves the same way, for example an active-orders row that contradicts a leg, because it latches FREEZE_INVARIANT, which is in _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP.
confirmed.evidence: 1484-1485: any open non-LATE_FILL store conflict adds 'HISTORY_CONFLICT' to tp_blockers globally. 117: _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP contains LEDGER_INVARIANT. 635-640: every StoreError/LedgerError in tick() sets FREEZE_INVARIANT, which only ack_history_conflict clears (1009). 1654-1661: when tp_blockers is non-empty, _act returns before the outside-bounds cancel collection (1663-1666) and before any TP dispatch. Scratch exp_conflict3.py printed: "store conflicts: [('OVERFILL', True)] state: FROZEN tp_blockers: ['HISTORY_CONFLICT']", "cell B E: 10 TP legs for B: 0 venue net: 10" and "outside bounds: cancels sent 0 entries still live: 9". exp_conflict2.py printed tp_blockers ['FROZEN:LEDGER_INVARIANT'] after one contradictory active row, with the same effects.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Scope TP blocking to the cells/CIDs named by the conflict or invariant. Keep dispatching TPs of unaffected cells whose history is exact. Keep sending risk-reducing entry cancels (outside bounds, TP priority) while frozen. Block only new entries globally.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. The engine code is the same in bcd2eebef and the current HEAD (bb49f434e), and every line the claim cites matches. engine.py:1484-1485 adds HISTORY_CONFLICT to tp_blockers for any open store conflict that is not a LATE_FILL. engine.py:117 puts LEDGER_INVARIANT in _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP. engine.py:635-640 latches FREEZE_INVARIANT on any StoreError or LedgerError in tick(), and only ack_history_conflict clears it (engine.py:1009). When tp_blockers is non-empty, engine.py:1654-1661 returns before the OUTSIDE_BOUNDS cancel collection at 1663-1666 and before any TP dispatch. The only cancels it still sends there are CANCEL_RETRY, so cancels are clearly considered safe in that state.

Reproduction: I ran a scratch test with the real Harness (FakeExchange plus the SQLite store), outside the repo. Cell A's venue order was given a larger amount, then filled 4 + 8 against a leg amount of 10. Results:
- State FROZEN, tp_blockers ['FROZEN:LEDGER_INVARIANT', 'HISTORY_CONFLICT'], conflicts ['OVERFILL'].
- Cell B's entry then fully filled: B E = 10, history_complete True. B had 0 TP legs after 60 ticks.
- Moving the book above upper_price produced 0 cancels, 9 entries still LIVE, and OUTSIDE_BOUNDS in the reasons.

So the scenario is concretely reachable. It needs a contradictory venue row, which AC-40 explicitly covers ("unknown owned fill"), or any store/ledger refusal.

Spec basis:
- NG-HIST-002 says a key with a different payload gives a "history conflict и pause".
- NG-OPS-001 says pause keeps servicing confirmed TP obligations unless a hard safety constraint is violated, and that a fill gap or unknown blocks only new exposure of the affected cell.
- AC-40 only requires that exposure stop.
- The spec's "freeze" consistently means entries: AC-30 freezes entries while TPs continue, and AC-32 is entries freeze/cancel.
- NG-OPS-002 and AC-32 say unconditionally that own active entries are cancel-requested outside bounds. A cancel reduces risk and needs no quantity guess, and the engine already sends CANCEL_RETRY in this state.
- The engine's own choice to keep TPs flowing under LATE_FILL, which the spec calls a whole-market freeze, weakens the argument that a non-late conflict is a hard safety constraint that justifies halting unrelated cells' TPs.

Mitigating points:
- The scanner-detected paths do not trigger this. With a payload conflict (inject_conflicting_trade) or trades exceeding the order cumulative, tp_blockers stayed [] and the outside-bounds cancels were sent (8 cancels in my run).
- Only store-level conflicts (OVERFILL, SIDE_MISMATCH, EXCHANGE_ID_MISMATCH, ORDER_MISMATCH and similar) and StoreError/LedgerError latches cause it.
- An operator audit is needed in these cases anyway.
- No wrong exposure is created: the effect is withheld TPs and stale entries left live.

For those reasons I lower the severity from high to medium.

confirmed.title: A drift check compares a position read taken before the same tick's history scan and raises a false 'position drift' RISK_BLOCKED
confirmed.requirement: NG-RISK-002/NG-RISK-003 (drift detection against the durable ledger), NG-CELL-001(5) (position and ledger reconciled), NG-OPS-001
confirmed.failure_scenario: B = 25 with a long cap of 30, so no BUY entry fits and 5 SELL entries rest (reachable interval [-25, 25]). A SELL entry fills 10 after the tick's account read but before its trades page is read, which is normal because REST reads are not atomic. The history commit makes P = 15 and P_max = 15, while the position read from moments earlier says 25. The engine marks manual_reconcile_required ('position drift: venue 25 outside ledger reachable [-25, 15]'). The engine goes RISK_BLOCKED and entries freeze until an operator baseline audit, even though venue and ledger both equal 15. This occurs whenever resting opposite-side remainder is below the fill quantity: near a cap, at a grid edge, or after outside-bounds cancels leave only one-sided TPs.
confirmed.evidence: The guard `self.position_at < self.last_history_commit_at` (1440-1441) is meant to skip positions that predate a committed fill. It is defeated because both values are the same tick-start `now`: 1081 `self.position_at = now` and 1290 `self.last_history_commit_at = now`. tick() reads the account (621) before scanning history (622), then runs _detect_drift (625) with no grace for out-of-interval values (1447-1452). Scratch exp_drift.py injects the fill between the two reads and printed: "venue net: 15 ledger P: 15", "manual_reconcile_required: True reason: position drift: venue 25 outside ledger reachable [-25, 15]" and "state: RISK_BLOCKED".
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compare only a position fetched after the latest history commit, using real read timestamps (self.clock() at read time) rather than tick-start. Alternatively require the out-of-interval condition to persist across a fresh position read plus a complete scan before marking drift.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The code at bcd2eebef matches the claim, and the scratch reproduction gives the claimed output on the worktree. engine.py has no changes between bcd2eebef and HEAD.

1. **The read order.** In `tick()`, `_refresh_account(now)` runs before `_scan_history(now)`. `_refresh_account` sets `self.position_at = now` (engine.py:1081). The history commit sets `self.last_history_commit_at = now` (engine.py:1290). Both use the same tick-start `now`.

2. **The guard cannot fire in this case.** `_detect_drift` (1440-1441) skips a position read that is older than the latest history commit (`self.position_at < self.last_history_commit_at`). The code comment says why: an older read "may predate a committed fill". When the position read and the commit happen in the same tick, the two timestamps are equal, so the check is false. The engine then compares a position read taken before the scan with a ledger that already includes fills from that scan.

3. **No grace period.** An out-of-interval value calls `mark_manual_reconcile_required` at once (1447-1452). That flag is sticky: only an operator baseline audit clears it (engine.py:880-885).

4. **Why the interval misses the stale value.** `self.endpoints` comes from `risk.endpoints_from_ledgers`, which counts only open legs. It does not count the owed TP that has not been placed yet. After a SELL fill of qty q, the new `P_max` is the old `P_max` minus q. The stale venue value (the old `P`) is therefore outside the interval whenever the resting BUY remainder is less than q. That happens with one-sided resting orders: near a cap, at or past a grid edge where only one side still rests, or when a sweep fills more than the opposite side's resting quantity.

5. **Reproduction.** I ran scratchpad/exp_drift.py with the repo on `PYTHONPATH`. Setup: B=25, cap 30, entry size 10. Before the fill, 5 SELL entries rested, no BUY entries rested, and the interval was [-25, 25]. The script injects a fill of 10 after the tick reads the position and before it reads the trades page. Output:
   - venue net 15, ledger P 15
   - manual_reconcile_required True, reason "position drift: venue 25 outside ledger reachable [-25, 15]"
   - state RISK_BLOCKED after 6 more ticks

6. **Real-world reachability.** On a real venue, the position, active-orders and trades reads are separate REST calls, so a fill can land between them.

**Spec impact.** Spec line 155 and AC-30 say a manual trade or real position drift freezes entries and needs an operator baseline audit. Here neither happened (venue equals ledger), yet entries freeze until an operator acts. That violates the drift semantics in NG-RISK-002 and NG-OPS-001. The engine's own guard comment shows the author meant to exclude this case.

**Severity.** It fails closed: TPs keep running and no funds are at risk. It is still a false, sticky entry freeze that operators must clear by hand, so medium is appropriate.

confirmed.title: A failing trading-rules refresh is retried every tick with no backoff, eats the weight budget and starves history scans, delaying TPs
confirmed.requirement: NG-HIST-003 (configurable weight limit and backoff with safe defaults; one engine, coalesced polling, no polling storm), AC-04, NG-CELL-002 (prompt TP after history)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Once rules are older than rules_refresh_s (60 s), a persistent failure of order_book_details (5xx, or 'market absent' raised by LighterExchangePort.trading_rules) makes the engine charge 300 weight and retry on every 1 s tick. In 120 s the engine made 54 rules calls and only 2 history scans (control run without the failure: 24 scans). History went stale, and a fully filled entry got its TP after 41 s instead of 1 s. Steady state already uses about 15,400 of the 16,200/min engine budget, so any un-backed-off retry starves scans and account polls.
confirmed.evidence: 1058-1066: the condition `self.rules is None or now - (self.rules_at or 0) >= rules_refresh_s`. It is re-evaluated each tick and rules_at is only updated on success, so there is no failure backoff. The HistoryScanner does have one (history.py _fail). Scratch exp_rules.py: {'order_book_details': 54, 'account': 24, 'active_orders': 24, 'inactive_orders': 2, 'trades': 2}, history stale, 'TP dispatched after 41.0 s'. exp_rules_control.py: 24 scans of each stream, 'TP dispatched after 1.0 s'. exp_weight.py, with defaults and one 1-lot fill every 3 s: 35 delayed scans, 15 delayed account polls, entries blocked by staleness in 19 of 180 ticks.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Record the attempt time on failure too, and back off exponentially (as the scanner does). Charge the rules refresh against a separate or lower-priority share so history scans and account polls keep their cadence.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. The code and a re-run both confirm it.

Code (engine.py:1058-1066, the same at bcd2eebef and in the worktree): `_refresh_account` runs first on every tick, before `_scan_history`. Each tick it checks `self.rules is None or now - (self.rules_at or 0) >= rules_refresh_s`. `rules_at` is set only on success (line 1064). On failure the code only logs RULES_UNAVAILABLE; it records no attempt time and applies no backoff. Each attempt is charged 300 against the shared engine budget (`weight_budget_per_min` = 16200) before the call. Nothing else throttles it:
- `EngineOptions` (data_types.py:32-42) has no rules backoff knob.
- `HistoryScanner` backs off only its own streams.
- The tests only flip `rules_available=False` (test_ng_engine_ops.py:69, test_ng_engine_risk.py:352) and never check cadence.

Why scans starve: with the defaults (poll 5 s, freshness 10 s) the steady load is about 12x600 for account+active plus 12x700 for one trades+inactive page each, roughly 15.6k of the 16.2k budget. The rules retry needs only 300 and runs first each tick, so it takes every bit of freed headroom. The 700 needed for a scan is almost never available.

Re-run: I ran the claimant's exp_rules.py and exp_rules_control.py with PYTHONPATH set to the worktree. I also ran a copy using pure default `EngineOptions()`, since the harness overrides `min_wake_interval_s`. All three matched the claim:
- Failure run: 54 order_book_details calls against only 2 trades and 2 inactive_orders calls in 120 s. History was stale, errors were RULES_UNAVAILABLE and WEIGHT_BUDGET, and the TP was dispatched 41 s after a full entry fill.
- Control run: 24 scans of each stream, and the TP was dispatched after 1 s.

The scenario is reachable in production. `LighterExchangePort.trading_rules` (lighter_port.py:303-325) raises on any failure of `_update_trading_rules`/`order_book_details`, and also when the market is absent.

Spec: NG-HIST-003 requires "weight limit and backoff configurable with safe defaults". Its wording is that exhaustion "delays new exposure, not proof". AC-04 forbids a polling storm. Here a failing non-proof endpoint is re-polled every tick with no backoff and pushes out the authoritative history scans. So proof is delayed, and TPs for fills already on the venue lag by about 40 s during an outage of one endpoint.

Why medium and not higher: behaviour stays fail-closed. Stale history blocks new entries, and the venue rate pool is not exceeded because `_can_spend` caps usage. The strict 2 s TP SLO in NG-CELL-002 and AC-14 is measured from the history commit, so the harm is the history-lag and backoff violation, not an unsafe order.

confirmed.title: After a runtime minimum decrease, ordinary partial fills make the router emergency-cancel other cells' resting entries for slots
confirmed.requirement: NG-RISK-002 (emergency entry cancel only for an unexpected venue order-cap drop or a hard-risk conflict, not to free slots that should be reserved; a regular partial fill is no reason to cancel an entry), NG-RISK-005 / AC-57 (no regular entry cancels or cancel spam), AC-34
confirmed.failure_scenario: 10 cells are armed with 3 slots each under cap 30 (floor 5). The venue lowers min_base/min_notional to 1; the cap is unchanged. Cell 3's entry then receives ordinary 1-lot partial fills. Each fill is split into its own TP at the new floor (TP 1, TP 1). The third TP needs a 4th slot, so the router cancels cell 9's resting entry ('SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY:tp:3:1:0'). Every further small fill on any armed cell can cancel another cell's entry.
confirmed.evidence: _act builds the budget from the admission plan (1688), which reports EXIT_RESERVATION_SHORTFALL with shortfall 8 per cell. It still hands the router every item of tp_obligation_to_dispatch split at the current floor (_tp_candidates 1627). When budget.take fails, router.py:258-275 cancel-requests another cell's LIVE entry. Nothing limits a cell's concurrent TP children to its reserved slots when the shortfall comes from a rules change rather than a cap drop. Scratch exp_minfall.py printed: "cancels: ['SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY:tp:3:1:0'] cancelled cells: [9] filled cell: 3" and "admission blocker: EXIT_RESERVATION_SHORTFALL".
confirmed.suggested_fix: When a cell's reservation is short because rules changed (not because the venue cap dropped), keep its extra obligation undispatched inside its reserved slots. For example, accumulate while the entry is live and dispatch in chunks no smaller than the arming-time minimum, and show it as a blocker. Reserve emergency entry cancels for an actual cap reduction or a hard-risk conflict.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. It reproduces against the real engine.

Code path:
- In engine.py `_act`, line 1688 builds `SlotBudget.from_plan(plan)` from the admission plan.
- `_tp_candidates` (line 1627) passes every item from `ledger.tp_obligation_to_dispatch(self.rules)` to the router. cells.py:509 dispatches the whole unassigned obligation at the current floor, so a 1-lot fill becomes a 1-lot TP.
- In router.py:258-275, when `budget.take` fails and no cancel is in flight, the router calls `select_entries_to_cancel(1, ...)` over all owned LIVE entries. It then sends a `SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY` cancel for the first one.
- admission.py records the rules-change deficit as `shortfall` and `EXIT_RESERVATION_SHORTFALL` (lines 153-162, 185-186). The engine has no reference to shortfall, so nothing limits a cell's TP children to its reserved slots. The router cannot tell a cap drop from a floor drop.

Spec:
- NG-RISK-002 says: "Регулярный partial fill не является причиной отменять entry. Emergency cancel entries допустим только при непредвиденном уменьшении venue order cap или hard-risk conflict, а не для освобождения слотов". Roughly: a regular partial fill is no reason to cancel an entry. Emergency entry cancels are allowed only for an unforeseen cut in the venue order cap or a hard-risk conflict, not to free slots.
- NG-RISK-005 and AC-34 expect runtime minimum changes, which should re-validate admission and restrict new entries.
- AC-57 forbids regular entry cancels and cancel spam.
- A lower minimum is neither a venue cap cut nor a hard-risk conflict.
- A compliant alternative exists: hold the extra obligation behind a visible blocker until one of the cell's TPs or its entry frees a slot. So the emergency cancel is not the only way to avoid starving the TP.
- The existing emergency test (test_ng_engine_risk.py:401) only covers a venue cap drop. The AC-34 test only covers a minimum increase.

Scratch run (harness, scratchpad script outside the repo, no repo changes):
- Setup: max_active_orders=30, 10 cells armed with 3 slots each, then the fake exchange's rules set to min_base=1 and min_notional=1.
- Admission printed `EXIT_RESERVATION_SHORTFALL`, shortfall 8 per cell, free=0.
- Cell 3 took two 1-lot fills, which became TPs [1, 1] in its reserved slots. The third fill caused `cancels: [('SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY:tp:3:1:0', 9)]`.
- An extended run showed it cascades. A second `SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY:tp:3:1:0` cancelled cell 8's entry. Cell 9 stayed queued and was not re-armed, because the admission blocker stayed `EXIT_RESERVATION_SHORTFALL`.
- So ordinary small fills after a minimum decrease steadily cancel resting entries on other cells and shrink the grid, against NG-RISK-002 and AC-57.
- The in-scope link is the engine's dispatch in `_act` / `_tp_candidates`, which drives the core router. Medium severity fits: it needs a runtime minimum decrease, which the spec expects, and it cancels entries without any fund-loss or self-trade risk.

confirmed.title: Rejected intents are re-issued with a new CID/revision every tick, with no backoff and no visible blocker
confirmed.requirement: NG-DB-005 (a new revision is allowed after config/rules are fixed), AC-34 (an unfulfillable TP becomes a visible blocker), AC-56, NG-HIST-004 (CID per revision)
confirmed.failure_scenario: (a) The venue changes tick size so the fixed TP price 5.4 is off-tick. Each tick the engine allocates a new CID, commits a durable TP intent plus reservation, and immediately marks it REJECTED_UNSENT (PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK): 32 dead TP legs for one obligation in 32 s, about 86k/day per obligation. The cell shows TP_REQUIRED with blocker None. (b) The venue persistently and definitively rejects one cell's entry with zero fill. The engine sends a new revision to the venue every tick: 61 submits and 61 CIDs in 60 s, while the engine reports NORMAL and the cell shows SETTLING with no blocker. Across 55 cells this is up to max_submits_per_tick=20 sends per second.
confirmed.evidence: _dispatch_intent records NOT_SENT for a pre-send blocker (1869-1875) but never sets cell_blockers or any retry gate. The TP obligation reappears in the next tick's _tp_candidates (1627) and gets a fresh identity/CID in _submit. For entries, _retry_only (128-132) turns the cycle idle in _slot_admission (1593-1597), so _idle_eligibility re-arms it the next tick. The only pre-send check at admission is _full_q_blocker (quantity only, not price tick). Scratch exp_tick.py: "TP legs for one obligation after 30 s: 32 states: ['REJECTED_UNSENT']", "cell state: TP_REQUIRED blocker: None". exp_reject.py: 61 venue rejects, 61 revisions (1,0)..(1,60), "cell state: SETTLING blocker: None", "engine: NORMAL []".
confirmed.suggested_fix: Latch a per-cell blocker with the rejection reason (for example PRESEND:PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK or VENUE_REJECT:<detail>) and do not create a new revision until trading rules or config actually change (compare fingerprints), or at least apply exponential backoff. Also check that grid prices are on the current tick in admission and TP planning.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. The code, the spec and two runs of my own all support it. I read engine.py at bb49f434e, which differs from bcd2eebef only by a flake8 fix in contracts.py.

**Code path**
- `_dispatch_intent` (engine.py:1865-1875) turns a `_pre_send_blocker` hit such as PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK into NOT_SENT / REJECTED_UNSENT. It never writes `cell_blockers`, a freeze, an engine reason or a retry gate.
- On the next tick, `_tp_candidates` (1627) sees the same unassigned obligation again. `_submit` (1793+) then allocates a new CID and TP revision, records a durable intent and reservation, and rejects it locally again.
- Nothing checks runtime tick-size changes before `_pre_send_blocker`:
  - `grid.rules_blockers` (grid.py:168) only checks that rules are well-formed.

- Setup: filled a BUY 5.3 entry, then changed the venue tick to 0.0007 so the fixed TP price 5.4 is off-tick.

- `test_ac56_presend_rejection_releases_only_without_transport` runs one tick only.
- `test_ac56_definitive_reject_allows_new_revision_timeout_does_not` only checks that revision 1 exists.

The spec says tick size comes from fresh runtime trading rules, and the engine re-reads them every 60 s. A tick change leaves open inventory whose TP is never placed. That method (lines 1919-1922) is the only code that dispatches PENDING cancel rows. I could not refute the claim. It holds, and the repro reproduces it. The engine.py I read is identical at HEAD bb49f434e and at the reviewed commit bcd2eebef; the only diff in the package is contracts.py.

**Why it happens (code evidence):**
- `store.record_cancel_intent` (store.py ~2897-2923) commits a CANCEL outbox row as PENDING and moves the leg to CANCEL_PENDING.
- Only `mark_dispatching` (store.py ~2888-2891) moves the leg from CANCEL_PENDING to CANCEL_UNKNOWN.
- In `engine._dispatch_cancels` (engine.py 1924-1954) these two steps are separate commits. - The trigger is narrow: a process death, or a persistence failure, exactly between two consecutive commits during the drain.

The operator or web UI sends baseline_audit action=resolve_unknown_submit. The gate `any(r.client_order_id == cid for r in (self.active_rows or []))` finds nothing, so the leg becomes REJECTED_ZERO_FILL. verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds. I read the code at bcd2eebef (engine.py is the same at the worktree HEAD bb49f434e) and reproduced it.

- The gate at engine.py:1027-1039 rejects only when `not self.history_complete`, the CID appears in `(self.active_rows or [])`, or the CID is in `terminal_rows`.
  - A failed fetch sets `active_rows = None` (line 1088). `or []` then turns "unknown" into "empty", so the check fails open.
  - Nothing compares `active_at` with the leg's dispatch time.
  - `history_complete` is only set True/False on scan outcomes (lines 1125/1132) and has no freshness check. `_cmd_baseline_audit` (line 859) does check `_history_stale` and `_position_stale`.
- The problem is wider than the claim says. `tick()` runs `_process_commands` (line 620) BEFORE `_refresh_account` (line 621). So when an audit is applied, `active_rows` always comes from an earlier poll. Right after a timed-out submit, that poll predates the dispatch.
- A landed resting TP creates no inactive-order or trade row. The pre-dispatch active list is therefore the only thing the gate consults for it, and it cannot contain the order.

Reproduction (scratch tests, read-only):
1. The reviewer's repro (active_orders failing) fails as described: two open SELL TPs of 10 for the cell.
2. My variant has NO fetch failure:

   - With 3 failed active fetches the engine even stays NORMAL for 12 ticks with both TPs resting.

The spec (NG-HIST-004) does allow "ручной аудит" (manual audit) as a way out of UNKNOWN. So this is a defect in the engine's own safety check (fail-open on stale or missing evidence), not an automatic path to a duplicate. It is still concretely reachable: an operator who resolves soon after a timeout, or while the active list is unavailable, gets a second TP with a new CID.

verdict.reasoning:

confirmed.title: Active rows fetched before the same tick's history commit are recorded as evidence, aborting ticks until the next poll and delaying TP dispatch

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. The code does what the claim says, and I reproduced it on its own. engine.py is identical at bcd2eebef and at the worktree HEAD bb49f434e, which changed only contracts.py.

How the failure happens:
1. In tick() (engine.py:621-623), `_refresh_account` fetches active_orders and then `_scan_history` runs.
2. `_apply_history` commits the terminal row, so the store now has venue_final=1 and venue_filled equal to the full amount. It also moves the leg to TERMINAL_UNKNOWN, which is not a final state.
3. `_reconcile_active` then works on the stale active row. It skips the TERMINAL_UNKNOWN->LIVE change for CIDs in terminal_rows. But the evidence path at line 1329-1331 still calls `record_order_evidence` whenever the (order_index, filled) cache key misses.
4. `store._order_row_problems` (store.py:3112-3117) flags "cumulative filled regressed" and "final order row changed". `record_order_evidence` raises InvalidTransitionError, which is a StoreError.
5. tick() catches it as STORE_REFUSED, sets FREEZE_INVARIANT in memory and sets reload_needed. The tick aborts before `_settle` and `_act`.
6. `_reload` (line 472-477) reloads meta from disk, so the freeze is transient. It also clears `_active_reconciled_at` and `_active_evidence_cache`. The same stale active_rows are therefore replayed on every tick until the next account poll (poll_interval_s=5).

Independent check: I wrote scratchpad/refute/test_refute_active_race.py with controls, using the repo's Harness and FakeExchange.
- Race with a prior partial fill (cache miss): the fill happens at t=15. There are 5 STORE_REFUSED errors with the message "InvalidTransitionError: order evidence for 1099511627777 conflicts: cumulative filled regressed 10 -> 3; final order row changed". The TP intent appears at t=21, 6 s after the history commit.
- Control without the race: TP at t=17.
- Race without a partial fill (cache hit): no refusal, TP at t=16.

So the trigger needs a cache miss. That happens after a new partial fill, on the first time an order appears in the active list, or after any `_reload`. Commands and `_act` errors also call `_reload`, which widens the window. All of these are normal in live operation. The race itself is an ordinary timing gap between two sequential REST reads in one tick, and the account poll and the history scan run on the same 5 s cadence.

This breaks the NG-CELL-002 / AC-14 SLO: the durable TP intent must reach the router no more than 2 s after the history fill commit. Here capacity, throttler and transport were all healthy, and the delay came only from the engine refusing its own stale evidence. It also creates spurious FROZEN states and STORE_REFUSED errors.

The code is in WS-D's scope (engine.py `_reconcile_active`). I found nothing elsewhere that handles this case. Medium severity fits: the TP is delayed by about one poll interval, not lost, and the engine recovers without operator action.

Suppose this tick's history batch commits an unmatched manual trade (a new store entry blocker) or fills that change P. A cell whose TP settlement completes in the same tick is still released as 'NG-CELL-001 release proven'. _detect_drift then sets position_reconciled=False only afterwards (1440-1443, 1458).

verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds. engine.py has the same content at bcd2eebef and at HEAD bb49f434e. `tick()` runs `_refresh_account → _scan_history → _reconcile_active → _settle → _detect_drift` (lines 620-625). `_settle` checks release with `ledger.can_release(self.position_reconciled)` (1398-1399) and then calls `self.cells[cell_id].release(self.position_reconciled)` (1415). `position_reconciled` is only assigned in `_detect_drift` (1437, 1443, 1458), so `_settle` always uses the value from the previous tick. - **Offsets 0-4:** the unmatched trade committed earlier, and cell 3 correctly stayed unreleased for all 40 ticks.
- **Offset 5:** the unmatched-trade commit landed in the same tick that the TP settlement finished. Cell 3 was released with flag_used=True while `store_entry_blockers` was already non-empty at `_settle` time. Right after that tick, `position_reconciled` was False with 1 store blocker.

- The released cell's own accounting is complete (E==X, cumulative equality, all legs terminal after settlement).
- In the store-blocker case, `_evaluate_state` still blocks new entries through STORE:* blockers.
- A baseline audit does not reopen cells.
- The worst real effect: for a plain position gap without a store blocker, POSITION_UNRECONCILED only blocks entries after `position_gap_grace_s`, so the prematurely released cell can re-enter in the same tick while venue != P. That is a spec-level violation with limited harm.

refuted.title: AC-38 test cannot detect a post-only to plain-LIMIT (taker) fallback; its order-type assertions are vacuous
refuted.why:
This is a test-strength point about a mutation that could happen, not a failure the current code can reach. It also reads AC-38 more broadly than the spec states it.

1) What AC-38 actually requires. Spec line 336 says a post-only rejection, dust, stale data or a TP blocker must not create a MARKET order. It does not forbid plain LIMIT. Spec line 48 (NG-ORD-001) explicitly allows LIMIT as a configured entry type in the "safe subset". Only MARKET, price clamping and TP distance gates are forbidden. A crossing LIMIT at the exact cell boundary is not a MARKET order and not clamping, so the claimed "post-only to LIMIT" fallback is outside AC-38's text.

2) The AC-38 check is not vacuous. MARKET cannot be expressed: contracts.py:89-92 has no MARKET member, and data_types.py:179 / grid.py:271 validate the config. engine.py:1766 `_pre_send_blocker` returns ORDER_TYPE_FORBIDDEN for anything else. FakeExchange records an "unsupported order type" violation for a non-policy type (fake_exchange.py:643), and test_ac38 asserts there is no such violation (test_ng_engine_risk.py:357). So a raw MARKET value sent by the engine would fail the test. The order_type membership assertion is redundant, but the test does guard the literal requirement.

3) The claimed failure cannot happen in the code under review. engine.py:1796 always uses `self.config.entry_order_type` for entries, and there is no downgrade path after a post-only cancel. `_idle_eligibility` (engine.py:1616-1619) blocks crossing entries with ENTRY_WOULD_CROSS before admission. When the venue lacks post-only support, entries are blocked with POST_ONLY_UNSUPPORTED rather than downgraded (engine.py:1515, 1773). The parametrized test test_untradable_market_blocks_new_exposure_and_presend covers that. The "10 of 11 non-post-only submits" result comes only from the reviewer's own mutated engine, not from the branch.

The only accurate residual point is documentation. ws-d-engine.md:109 overstates coverage by calling Harness.assert_safe_orders a "global check in every harness run". In fact it runs in only test_ac01 and test_ac02, plus the per-step order-type check in the property checker. That is a low-severity trace wording issue, not a behaviour defect or an AC-38 violation.

refuted.title: NG-HIST-003 weight-budget exhaustion and WS-burst coalescing are never exercised; the AC-04 weight assertion holds even without enforcement
refuted.why:
This claim is about missing tests, not wrong behaviour. The claimant's own probe shows the shipped engine meets NG-HIST-003: with a 4000/min budget it reads only 4 pages per minute and goes HISTORY_STALE/DEGRADED. Its failure scenario only happens if someone removes the guard ("if `_can_spend` were removed"), so it cannot occur in the code under review.

What the code does:
- **Per-minute cap.** `_can_spend` (engine.py:675-676) compares the rolling 60 s ledger with `weight_budget_per_min`. The default is 16200, 90% of the 18000/min pool (data_types.py:34).
- **Account poll.** It is skipped with a WEIGHT_BUDGET error when the budget is exhausted (engine.py:1074-1076).
- **History scan.** It returns early before any scan (engine.py:1096-1099). History then goes stale and HISTORY_STALE blocks entries (engine.py:1500-1501). A complete-scan record is written only when a scan actually completes, so exhaustion delays new exposure and never skips proof.

The coalescing half of the claim is wrong:
- `NeutralGridEngine.wake()` (engine.py:574-586) only calls `scanner.wake()`. Coalescing is done by HistoryScanner using `min_wake_interval_s` (history.py:413).
- That behaviour is tested where it lives. `test_failures_back_off_and_wakeups_coalesce` sends 10 wakes and gets one scan. `test_concurrent_scans_are_coalesced` checks that parallel scans are merged. `test_ac12_break_before_boundary_is_incomplete_and_resumes` checks that one call's work stays bounded (budget 700 means one page per stream).
- All three are listed in the WS-C trace for NG-HIST-003. The harness setting `min_wake_interval_s = tick` does not make coalescing unverified overall.

On scope: NG-HIST-003 and the ACs mapped to it (AC-04, AC-13) specify behaviour; none requires a budget-exhaustion test. AC-04 asks for no per-cell tasks or threads and no polling storm. `test_ac04` checks exactly that: no extra threads or tasks, account polls at the coalesced cadence, a bounded scan count and unique CIDs. The review brief rules out "consider adding" items, and this is one.

Residual note, low at most: no engine-level test drives `weight_budget_per_min` to exhaustion, so the WS-D trace row for NG-HIST-003 is thinner than it claims. That is a coverage gap, not a defect.

refuted.title: AC-04 'no per-cell tasks' assertion is vacuous
refuted.why:
The claim overstates the problem, and the mutation it relies on does not break AC-04.

1. **Only half the assertion is vacuous.** The claim is right that `tasks_before == 0` at test_ng_engine_risk.py:94/100 always holds, because the harness loop only runs inside `run_until_complete`. The other half, `not asyncio.all_tasks(h.loop)`, does real work. `asyncio.all_tasks(loop)` returns every task that is not done, including on a loop that is not running.
   - I checked this with the project venv. After `run_until_complete` of a tick that creates 55 long-lived tasks, `all_tasks` returns 55, so the assertion fails.
   - After a tick that gathers 55 short tasks and awaits them, `all_tasks` returns 0.
   - Together with the `threading.active_count()` check, the test does catch the pattern AC-04 is about: long-lived tasks or threads, one per cell.

2. **The spec does not forbid the passing mutation.** AC-04 (spec line 302) says: «При N=55 нет 55 executor tasks/потоков и polling storm; один engine пакетирует работу». In English: at N=55 there are no 55 executor tasks or threads and no polling storm, and one engine batches the work.
   - That targets per-cell executors, meaning control loops that stay alive, and polling storms. It does not target coroutines that are gathered and finished within one tick.
   - Tasks that are gathered and awaited inside the engine's single tick are still one engine batching the work.
   - The polling-storm half is checked separately with real counts: `weight_log` account polls ≤ 7 in 30 s, `page_log` scans bounded, and the weight budget. Per-cell tasks that did any polling would fail those checks.
   - The executor-count half is covered by the controller test `test_controller_creates_exactly_one_executor_and_never_recreates`, which the trace (ws-d-engine.md:75) lists next to this test.

3. **Nothing in production is affected.** A grep of `neutral_grid_executor/*.py` finds no `create_task`, `ensure_future`, `gather`, `Thread` or `run_in_executor`. The engine is one `async tick()`, which matches CONTRACTS.md:50.

Net result: one dead variable in a test. It is not a reachable AC-04 violation and not a wrong-behaviour defect.

refuted.title: The launcher drain reports a clean stop for a fail-closed engine, and its 90 s timeout precedes the engine's 120 s STOP_UNCERTAIN
refuted.why:
I checked bcd2eebef; the script and executor.py are the same at HEAD bb49f434e.

Scope: this review covers "WS-D engine part 1" and names neutral_grid_executor/{engine,executor,fake_exchange,commands,snapshot,data_types}.py plus the engine tests. The claim is anchored in scripts/lighter_robinhood_fixed_neutral_grid.py, which is not on that list. NG-OPS-003 and AC-36 are also not among the focus ACs. The claim is outside this review's scope.

The claim also fails on substance. The spec does not allow reporting a stop as successful when it is uncertain. Nothing in either scenario reports a success.

(a) Fail-closed engine. fatal_reason is set only when the engine is built: STORE_OPEN_REFUSED or NO_STORE (engine.py:197, 238) and STORE_LOAD_FAILED (engine.py:314). It is never set during a run. A fail-closed engine therefore never ran in this process. executor.on_start returns early (executor.py:124-127) without taking CID ownership. The engine placed and tracked no orders, and it has no writable store in which to record a stop outcome. The fail-closed reason is logged as an error at start, and status_text shows it. The drain's boolean return is ignored by on_stop (script:154); only test_neutral_grid.py:375 reads it. No log or record says the stop was clean, and the executor is detached before V2 persistence, so no EARLY_STOP record is stored either.

(b) Timeout at 90 s versus 120 s. On timeout the launcher logs a warning that the stop was not proven and force-stops the executor. It does not report a success. The durable state stays STOPPING with stop_outcome None. That is not STOPPED, so AC-48 (no optimistic NORMAL/STOPPED) is met. AC-36 is met: a CANCEL_UNKNOWN or SUBMIT_UNKNOWN leg gives STOP_UNCERTAIN at once (engine.py:1965-1967, test_ac36_stop_with_unknown_cancel_is_stop_uncertain_and_restart_keeps_reconciling). The 90-120 s gap only affects legs still waiting on history, which the engine's own rule does not yet treat as uncertain. On the next start, the launcher's START command clears stop_requested_ms and stop_outcome (engine.py:726-731). So a durable STOP_UNCERTAIN instead of STOPPING would change nothing in reconciliation.

What remains is a launcher mismatch: the drain timeout is shorter than stop_uncertain_after_s, and the warning text says the durable state is STOP_UNCERTAIN when it is STOPPING. That is a low-impact item for the launcher/ops part of the review, not a violation of NG-OPS-003 in this scope.
